format: Situation (under 20 seconds) → what you decided and what you rejected → result with a number → one line on why it matters for this role. About 2 minutes out loud.
rubric: Situation set in under 20 seconds, with scale (users, data, team)
Named the decision you made and at least one alternative you rejected
Result stated with a concrete number (time, money, users, incidents, latency)
Tied back to this role: agents, AWS, security or client work

stories.title: Owning the Moveo ERP end to end
stories.brief: Taking over after a management change; HR, payroll and tender modules; now the company's main management system with about 50 daily users.
stories.answers: "architect → build → deploy → refine" and "real value, not prototypes"
prompts: What state was the system in when you took it over, and what did you decide to fix first?
Which architectural decision would you defend today, and which would you reverse?
What number proves it delivered value: users, hours saved, errors removed?

stories.title: Your agentic AI and MCP work
stories.brief: The most relevant story and currently the vaguest. For each server or workflow: what it does, which model, who uses it, what it saved.
stories.answers: "Tell me about your MCP work" and every agentic-AI depth question
prompts: Name each MCP server or workflow and the one problem it solves.
Which model and why? What broke the first time, and what did you change?
Who uses it today and what does it save them per week?

stories.title: Security in a sensitive-data system
stories.brief: Roles, permissions and audit logging in the payroll module. Transfers directly to the agent access-control and audit-trail questions.
stories.answers: "How do you stop an agent leaking documents?" and governance questions
prompts: How were roles and permissions modelled, and where were they enforced?
What did the audit log record, and did anyone ever actually use it?
How would you apply the same design to an agent that retrieves documents?

stories.title: A hard technical problem
stories.brief: A performance tuning win, or a Kafka or Elasticsearch issue, with before and after numbers.
stories.answers: "Tell me about a hard technical problem"
prompts: What was the symptom and how did you narrow it down?
What did you try that did not work?
Before and after numbers: latency, throughput, cost, error rate.

stories.title: Government and private clients at InterAdria
stories.brief: Shows you have handled client requirements, close to the professional-services setting they prefer.
stories.answers: "Have you worked with clients?" and consulting-fit questions
prompts: A requirement that changed late, and how you handled the client conversation.
How you translated a vague request into a scoped deliverable.
What a government client cared about that a private one did not.

stories.title: Mentoring and code review
stories.brief: What you changed in how juniors work.
prompts: One concrete habit you changed in a junior's work and how you did it.
What your code reviews look for first.
Evidence it worked: fewer review rounds, fewer production bugs, faster onboarding.

stories.title: A mistake
stories.brief: Something that broke in production and what you changed afterward.
prompts: What broke, who noticed, and how long until it was fixed?
Your part in it, stated plainly.
The process or technical change that stops it recurring.

extra.title: The age and Senior title question
extra.note: Answer with scope of ownership, not years: systems owned end to end, users served, decisions made alone, people mentored.
